text:
mike: Quick follow-up on compaction RFC. Canary shows small-batch tail spikes correlated with compactor runs.

tera: saw same in staging. compactor walk seems to hog CPU and generate pagefault churn.

josh: do we have a minimal repro? is this memcpy+remap under a global slab lock?

mike: repro: steady 6-8 concurrent short requests (64-128 tokens). When compaction runs we observe 40-80ms pauses. Logs: [compactor] walk shard=2; candidates=900 | [alloc] stall: waiting for staging slots; active_batches=6 | [pfault] spike: 100/s -> 780/s | [compactor] finish; reclaimed=12MB

sophia: PF spike implies we tear mappings during moves. Current flow: alloc dest slab -> memcpy pages -> publish mapping -> free old slab, done under arena-global lock.

tara: global lock is terrible for latency-sensitive tiny batches. Proposal: incremental micro-moves + cooperative yielding.

eva: also tenant-aware avoidance: don't compact slabs for tenants currently in high-SLO windows.

josh: we need a hotset estimator. We can reuse kvcache sampling to score slabs and tenants.

mike: implementation sketch: background_compactor ticks every 200ms, prioritized queue of (tenant, slab, score). Each tick do up to M slabs and up to K pages per micro-move. Publish via atomic pointer swap; free old pages only after GPU-fence epoch observed.

sophia: pointer-swap is fine but requires tying free to GPU epoch/RC so in-flight kernel descriptors don't reference freed pages.

tara: add exponential backoff + token-bucket budget so compaction throttles on p99 increase.

josh: beware global fragmentation shifting cost: avoiding high-SLO tenants can increase fragmentation on low-SLO tenants, raising offload churn. Value function: reclaimed_bytes - (pf_cost + latency_penalty). Only compact when net_benefit > 0.

eva: console knobs proposal: compaction.mode={aggressive,balanced,conservative}, compaction.slo_avoidance={true,false}, plus tenant.meta.compact_priority float. Defaults: balanced + slo_avoidance=true for Dedicated clusters.

mike: correctness notes for micro-move publish: 1) allocate dest pages; 2) pin source pages; 3) memcpy; 4) publish new mapping via atomic swap; 5) unpin and free old after fence. This avoids the arena-global lock but needs a short pin window.

sophia: add tests around publish-failure mid-move and concurrent GPU-epoch delays.

tara: test plan: canary cluster-A = current compactor, cluster-B = incremental prioritized compaction. Measure p99, offload-rate, reclaimed_bytes, cost/token. Include synthetic small-batch workload + mixed real trace.

mike: timeline: prototype 2w, canary 1m. infra-bot: feature flag ff/compactor_incremental for rollout.

infra-bot: feature flag created: ff/compactor_incremental

eva: I can wire console knobs once API is stable.

josh: remember fault-injection test for publish failing mid-move to ensure no UAF.

sophia: also stress GPU epoch latency under many small concurrent moves.

tara: :thumbsup: actionable.

mike: I'll open the follow-up RFC with algorithm, micro-move API, telemetry/backoff rules, and tests. Patch incoming.
